key_step: Riemann sum with t=2^n, improper integral of (1-x)^-1/2
justification: Recognising the sum as a Riemann sum with an integrable endpoint singularity; a single familiar move.

key_step: Period 2 reduction; two floor functions on one period
justification: Two different greatest-integer layers must be tabulated on one period and the period of the sum identified; routine multi-step chain with option-based format, no unfamiliar idea. Nearest anchor 2021-P2-Q19 (L4) is a numerical question with unknown breakpoints, so this sits well below it.

key_step: Riemann sum gives a=pi/2; f=tan(x/2); evaluate at pi/4
justification: Three routine stages (limit of a sum, half-angle simplification, derivative and surd arithmetic) with no new idea and options to check against. Comparable to routine two-concept chains rated 2.

key_step: Period pi/2 reduces to (sin x+cos x)^2 on [0,pi/2]
justification: One familiar periodicity trick followed by a one-line integral. Equivalent to a king-property-style single move.

key_step: a=-1 from one-sided limits; f is constant on unit intervals
justification: Needs the one-sided limits of two floor terms and then four unit-interval evaluations; routine multi-step with careful floor bookkeeping but no insight, with options.

key_step: Bound g(x)/x via concavity of g with g(0)=0 (monotone g/x)
justification: Bounding an integral needs the less-practised idea that g/x is monotone when g is concave with g(0)=0; the intended solution also hides an invalid step, so a careful student must check the options by actual bounds. Nearest anchor is the series-bound inequality statements (L3).

key_step: Slopes of piecewise-linear f and trapezoid areas
justification: Two short statements, each a routine check (derivative of moduli, area of a polyline); needs both but neither needs an idea. Below the multi-correct statement anchors because it is single-correct.

key_step: Split at x=3/2; integrate [t] over unit intervals
justification: Modulus of a quadratic plus a shifted greatest-integer function; two independent routine computations summed, options available.

key_step: By parts + t^2=(t^2+5)-5 gives the reduction formula; I_5'=(x^2+5)^-5
justification: Standard reduction-formula derivation (by parts, rewrite, rearrange) followed by recognising I_5' via FTC; long-ish but familiar chain with options. Rated 2 rather than 3 because the technique is heavily practised.
One standard substitution leading to arctan; the tan(x/2) substitution is the single familiar move.
